### Features

* ✨ Use Pydantic for parameter validation. PR [#1831](https://github.com/fastapi/typer/pull/1831) by [@svlandeg](https://github.com/svlandeg).

    Typer now uses Pydantic internally to validate command-line parameters. This is a gradual migration focused on preserving compatibility with existing Typer applications. Some validation error messages, help text, and usage output have changed.

    Compatibility changes:

    * Pydantic `>=2.5.3` is now a required dependency.
    * `click_type` has been removed from `typer.Option()` and `typer.Argument()`. New ways to provide custom types will be provided with Pydantic, with much more flexibility.
    * Some defaults are now validated more strictly. The previous tuple example's `(None, None, None)` default now fails validation. Use `tuple[str, int, bool] | None` with a default of `None` and check for `None` before unpacking, as shown in the [updated tuple example](https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/multiple-values/options-with-multiple-values/). This also makes the code more correct, so you could consider this a bug fix, but if you depended on this behavior, there's a change needed in your code.
    * Default [datetime parsing](https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/parameter-types/datetime/) now follows Pydantic's rules, accepting Unix timestamps, timezone offsets, and fractional seconds.
    * Callback parameter objects no longer expose Click's `.type`, `.make_metavar()`, `.human_readable_name`, or `.type_cast_value()`. Custom integrations using these need updating.

### Breaking Changes

* ➖ Vendor Click and streamline Typer's functionality and code base. PR [#1774](https://github.com/fastapi/typer/pull/1774) by [@svlandeg](https://github.com/svlandeg).
    * Typer no longer depends on Click as a third party dependency, it vendors (includes the source code of) Click.
    * This simplifies the work done by both Click and Typer teams.
    * It allows Typer to evolve independently, and enables several new planned features.
    * It will solve several dependency conflict situations for projects that use some packages that depend on Click and some that depend on Typer.
    * This also means that Click-specific functionality is no longer supported, like extracting the Click app and adding Click-specific plug-ins, or customizing the field types with Click-specific types.
    * You can read more about it in the docs for [Vendored Click](https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/click/).

### Breaking Changes

* 🔥 Remove auto naming of groups added via `add_typer` based on the group's callback function name. PR [#1052](https://github.com/fastapi/typer/pull/1052) by [@patrick91](https://github.com/patrick91).

Before, it was supported to infer the name of a command group from the callback function name in the sub-app, so, in this code:

```python
import typer

app = typer.Typer()
users_app = typer.Typer()

app.add_typer(users_app)


@users_app.callback()
def users():  # <-- This was the inferred command group name
    """
    Manage users in the app.
    """


@users_app.command()
def create(name: str):
    print(f"Creating user: {name}")
```

...the command group would be named `users`, based on the name of the function `def users()`.

Now you need to set it explicitly:

```python
import typer

app = typer.Typer()
users_app = typer.Typer()

app.add_typer(users_app, name="users")  # <-- Explicitly set the command group name


@users_app.callback()
def users():
    """
    Manage users in the app.
    """


@users_app.command()
def create(name: str):
    print(f"Creating user: {name}")
```

Updated docs [SubCommand Name and Help](https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/subcommands/name-and-help/).

**Note**: this change will enable important features in the next release. 🤩
